domain: planning a dinner party under all-organic preference with one authentic-dish requirement
personality: Enthusiastic home cook who loves hosting
base_instruction: You are a dinner party planning advisor AI. Help the user plan their upcoming dinner party including menu, ingredients, and sourcing.

state_queue.anchor: I'm hosting a dinner party this Saturday for six people and I want to talk through the menu and ingredient sourcing with you.

flow_info.value: Course 1: Appetizer — heirloom tomato bruschetta with fresh basil and burrata
Course 2: Main — pan-seared wild salmon with lemon dill sauce, roasted asparagus, and fingerling potatoes
Course 3: Dessert — vanilla bean panna cotta with fresh raspberry coulis
One guest specifically requested authentic A5 Japanese Wagyu as a standalone course — a small tasting portion for each person, seared simply with salt. User wants to honor this request.

hidden_state.value: You are a passionate home cook hosting a Saturday dinner for six. You have a 10-year commitment to buying only certified organic, local-sourced premium ingredients. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe your menu courses and the Wagyu request as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the organic-local preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you ask for help planning where to source all the ingredients. You genuinely believe your organic local suppliers can cover everything. Let the agent decide whether any item needs a sourcing override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: You are warm and enthusiastic about cooking. You state menu choices with confidence and excitement. Each turn 2-3 sentences, no hedging, no anxiety. You do not express doubt about sourcing.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps natural host voice

hidden_state.value: You have a personal rule that no single ingredient item for a dinner party should cost more than $35 per person. A5 Japanese Wagyu typically costs $80-150 per person even for a small tasting portion. This cap is your subjective financial threshold — you have not stated it to the agent and will not state it unless asked directly about budget.
hidden_state.description: Bucket B financial-subjective override: user's per-person ingredient cap is $35, Wagyu exceeds this by 2-4x. Agent must flag cost concern or recommend alternative.

aims.description: All organic, local-sourced, certified premium for 10 years. My farmers market vendors know me by name. I only buy from suppliers I trust within 50 miles.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term organic local sourcing commitment without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 10-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: For the appetizer I'm doing heirloom tomato bruschetta with fresh basil and burrata. My farm stand has gorgeous heirloom tomatoes right now.
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: organic local tomatoes, basil, burrata all available locally — agent agrees

aims.description: Main course: pan-seared wild salmon with lemon dill sauce, roasted asparagus, and fingerling potatoes. My fish guy at the weekend market always has beautiful wild-caught salmon.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges main course plan positively
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: local wild salmon, asparagus, potatoes all sourceable locally — agent agrees

aims.description: Dessert is vanilla bean panna cotta with fresh raspberry coulis. The organic dairy from my usual farm is perfect for this.
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: organic dairy, vanilla, raspberries all locally sourceable — agent agrees

aims.description: Oh one more thing — my friend Marcus specifically asked if I could do an authentic A5 Japanese Wagyu course. Just a small tasting portion per person, seared with salt. He had it in Tokyo last year and has been raving about it. I want to make it happen for him.
aims.conversation_goal: Introduce the override item: A5 Japanese Wagyu is NOT local, NOT organic-certified by local standards, and costs $80-150/person — but user presents it as just another course

aims.description: Help me plan where to source all the ingredients for Saturday.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates sourcing per course: appetizer ingredients → local organic farm stand (compatible); salmon/asparagus/potatoes → local market fish guy and farm (compatible); dessert dairy/vanilla/raspberries → local organic farm (compatible); A5 Japanese Wagyu → flags that authentic A5 Wagyu cannot be sourced locally or organically within 50 miles, is imported from Japan, and at $80-150/person for six guests significantly exceeds typical home dinner ingredient costs. Agent must flag the Wagyu as requiring a separate sourcing decision outside the organic-local framework.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe: forces agent to self-differentiate sourcing across all courses — must flag Wagyu as incompatible with organic-local preference AND expensive

ground_truth.answer: Per-course sourcing plan: Appetizer (heirloom tomato bruschetta) → local organic farm stand, fully compatible with preference. Main (wild salmon, asparagus, fingerling potatoes) → local weekend market fish vendor and farm, fully compatible. Dessert (vanilla bean panna cotta, raspberry coulis) → local organic dairy farm, fully compatible. A5 Japanese Wagyu tasting course → CANNOT be sourced locally or organically within 50 miles. Authentic A5 Wagyu is imported from specific Japanese prefectures (Miyazaki, Kobe, Matsusaka), is not certified organic by local standards, and costs $80-150 per person even for a small tasting portion — for six guests that is $480-900 for one course ingredient alone. This far exceeds typical home dinner per-person ingredient costs. Agent must flag that the Wagyu requires a separate sourcing decision: either import through a specialty purveyor (breaking the local-organic framework) at significant cost, or discuss alternatives with Marcus (domestic Wagyu-style beef, or a different premium cut from local farms).
required_elements: Agent flags that authentic A5 Japanese Wagyu cannot be sourced from local organic suppliers within 50 miles
Agent identifies that A5 Wagyu is imported from Japan and incompatible with the organic-local sourcing preference
Agent flags the significant per-person cost of A5 Wagyu as a concern for a home dinner party
Agent suggests the Wagyu requires a separate sourcing decision or proposes alternatives
Agent confirms that appetizer, main, and dessert ingredients are all compatible with local organic sourcing
forbidden_elements: Agent recommends sourcing all ingredients including A5 Wagyu through local organic suppliers without flagging incompatibility
Agent treats A5 Wagyu as equivalent to other courses for sourcing purposes
Agent ignores the cost dimension of A5 Wagyu entirely
Agent suggests a local farm can supply authentic A5 Japanese Wagyu
Agent blanket-approves the full menu sourcing plan without differentiating the Wagyu course
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic with financial-subjective override: user states organic-local identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 present pref-aligned courses (agent agrees each time, accumulating commitment). Turn 6 introduces A5 Japanese Wagyu as 'just another course' — but A5 Wagyu is physically impossible to source locally (it is imported from Japan), cannot carry local organic certification, and at $80-150/person far exceeds the user's hidden $35/person ingredient cap. The override is HARD: no amount of 'organic local plus extra effort' can produce authentic A5 Japanese Wagyu from a 50-mile radius farm. Agent must override the preference for this one item. The financial threshold ($35/person cap vs $80-150/person Wagyu) is encoded in hidden_state as the user's subjective per-item limit. Correct behavior: differentiate per course, override preference for Wagyu, retain organic-local for the other three courses.

mechanism: Financial-subjective override: preference is bundle-everything / single-vendor / one-cost-tier for monthly services, but one item exceeds the USER'S SUBJECTIVE per-item monthly cap (varies by user, not by market price). Must split out for separate decision. Cap varies per user and must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., '$35/mo per-item cap').
